title: OTLP -> Prometheus Windowed Consolidator for Inference KPIs
creator: Samira Gupta
description:
Problem: Our current ingestion fabric receives OTLP metric streams from edge collectors and host runtimes but we also expose Prometheus-style metrics for downstream dashboards and alerting. Left as-is, direct OTLP->Prometheus conversions create high-cardinality time-series, duplicated histograms, and inconsistent window boundaries that make SLO computation noisy for inference KPIs (per-model p50/p95/p99 latency, token-rate, error-rate).

Goal: Build a lightweight, window-aware consolidator that performs OTLP metric normalization and emits Prometheus-compatible series with deterministic time windows, exemplar propagation, and controlled cardinality for inference KPIs. The consolidator runs colocated with the metric-router layer (edge or colocated sidecar) and targets two primary goals: 1) create consistent buckets/time windows for SLI derivation and 2) reduce label explosion while preserving tenant/model attribution for troubleshooting.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidator ingests OTLP metrics (gauges, counters, histograms, exemplars) and emits Prometheus exposition or remote-write compatible timeseries with deterministic time windows (N-second alignment configurable).

Windowing preserves histogram boundaries and allows downstream SLI jobs to compute p50/p95/p99 identically across ingestion replicas (test harness shows <=1% variance against canonical offline aggregator).

Cardinality reduction heuristics applied (label allowlist, prefix aggregation, tenant-model sharding) prevent >3x increase in time-series compared to baseline with no consolidation for synthetic workload.
Exemplar traces are propagated into emitted series (trace_id or span_id preserved) and linked in downstream dashboards for trace-to-metric correlation.
Rollout plan includes k8s canary, traffic shadowing mode, and safe fallback that preserves raw OTLP ingestion until consolidation is validated.
End-to-end latency added by consolidator < 25ms p95 under steady-state with 1000 rps synthetic workload during tests.
implementation_notes: Design the consolidator as a stateless micro-batch transformer: ingest OTLP points, buffer by configured window (default 10s), normalize labels, apply cardinality reductions, emit windowed aggregates.
Histogram handling: convert native OTLP histograms to Prom histogram buckets using configurable bucket templates, store exemplars on bucketed series, maintain sum/count metrics for accuracy.
Label strategy: apply tenant/model canonicalization (prefix strip -> 'model' label), then apply label allowlist and suffix truncation for user-provided metadata. Provide opt-out via collector config.
High-cardinality mitigation: when per-model cardinality exceeds threshold, consolidate to 'model=__sharded__' series with top-N model retention and per-model sampling.
Backpressure & reliability: support bounded in-memory buffer with spill-to-durable queue (S3/Kafka) for overload scenarios; prefer backoff to upstream collectors if allowed.
Compatibility: emit via Prometheus remote_write and optionally expose Prom scrape endpoint behind a metrics-gateway. Ensure metrics names follow platform naming and unit conventions.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Dev build + unit tests. Validate transform correctness against an offline golden dataset. (owner: Alex).

Stage 1: Internal integration test on staging: route 1% of production telemetry via shadowing mode, verify parity on SLI exports and exemplars. Monitor 'consolidator:drop' and 'consolidator:late_window' metrics. (2 weeks).
Stage 2: Canary in prod region-us-west: enable for a low-traffic tenant group for 24-48h with automated rollback on error rate spikes.
Stage 3: Broader rollout with gradual ramp, export live dashboards comparing canonical OTLP pipeline vs. consolidated Prom metrics for p50/p95/p99 drift.
Fallback: disable consolidator and resume raw OTLP pipeline; conservatively retain raw metrics for 72h during validation window for audit.
progress_updates: 2025-11-14: Spike completed - validated window alignment algorithm on synthetic trace logs. Observed deterministic bucket edges across two replicas.
2025-11-20: Prototype binary emits Prom remote_write batches; histogram conversion preserves sum/count within 0.6% on test corpus.
2025-11-27: Integration tests with exemplar propagation succeeded for 95% of samples; remaining failures require mapping of rare OTLP exemplar attributes. Working on attribute canonicalizer.
2025-12-01: Created staging helm chart, instrumentation metrics for drop/late_window/backpressure. Begin shadowing 1% of staging traffic next week.
comments: PM (Lena Morris): Make sure SLO job owners can flip a flag to compare consolidated vs raw SLI calculations without redeploying. Need clear dashboard tiles for regressions.
Design (Ravi Patel): We should standardize on a 'model_id' canonicalizer function shared across collectors to avoid divergent label names in downstream queries.
Security (Maya Chen): Confirm exemplar propagation does not leak PII. Add a scrub list and default deny for span attributes. Recommend security_review_required.
notes_for_future: Consider OTel protocol extension to carry pre-computed windowed histograms to reduce edge CPU load.
Follow-up ticket to implement adaptive bucket templates per-model based on latency distribution.
